title: Dinosaurs May Have Been Literally Charbroiled After the Asteroid Impact
gist: The cause of the dinosaurs' extinction — the Chicxulub asteroid — is settled, but the kill mechanism is not: a 'fire' global-firestorm scenario competes with an 'ice' impact-winter scenario. A new Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences study by Purdue planetary scientists modelling the vaporized ejecta plume revives the fire case after years in which impact winter held the edge.

insights.claim: The cause of the dinosaur extinction is settled — a massive asteroid struck the Yucatan Peninsula and formed the Chicxulub crater — but the mechanism by which the animals actually died remains contested.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Separating a settled cause from an unsettled mechanism is the useful frame: consensus on the trigger does not mean consensus on the transmission channel.
insights.quote: We know why the dinosaurs died—a massive asteroid hit the Yucatan Peninsula forming the Chicxulub crater—but how they died is still the subject of debate.
insights.locator: We know why the dinosaurs died

insights.claim: The 'ice' extinction scenario holds that a cloud of impact dust blotted out the sun enough to drop global temperatures, analogous to a nuclear winter.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: The impact-winter model is the same physics invoked in nuclear-winter and geoengineering debates, so evidence shifts here echo into climate-intervention arguments.
insights.quote: a cloud of dust from the impact blotted out the sun enough to cause a drop in global temperatures (similar to a nuclear winter)

insights.claim: The 'fire' extinction scenario holds that material ejected by the impact rained back down through the atmosphere and ignited a global firestorm that cooked almost everything alive.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A firestorm kills on a timescale of hours to days rather than years, implying an entirely different extinction-selectivity pattern in the fossil record.
insights.quote: As material ejected from the impact rained down from the atmosphere, it ignited a global firestorm, essentially cooking almost everything alive.
insights.locator: The “fire” scenario is much more violent

themes.theme: Purdue plume modelling revives the firestorm case

insights.claim: After years in which the impact-winter explanation held the edge among researchers, a new study in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences pushes the global-firestorm explanation back into contention.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: A live example of a scientific consensus reversing on modelling improvements rather than new field evidence.
insights.quote: While Team Ice has seemed to have an edge in recent years, Team Fire is coming in hot with a new study
insights.locator: While Team Ice has seemed to have an edge

insights.claim: Planetary scientists at Purdue University modelled the physical characteristics of the enormous plume of vaporized material that the Mt. Everest-sized Chicxulub asteroid displaced into the upper atmosphere.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: The debate now turns on plume physics in the upper atmosphere — the same modelling domain used for asteroid-deflection and atmospheric-injection risk assessment.
insights.quote: It’s the physical characteristics of that plume and immediate aftermath that planetary scientists from Purdue University were focused on modeling in this latest study.
